messages:
anya: Heads-up — onboarding opalynx-embed v1.0 (int6 export) showed a surprising recall@10 regression on our short-query SEQA holdout. FP16 baseline recall@10 = 0.842, int6 = 0.780 (~6.2% absolute). quick triage thread.

maria: ugh. can you paste the eval command and a short snippet of the numbers?

anya: sure — ran locally on a 10k holdout. command: 
```
./eval_embeddings.py --model opalynx-1.0-int6 --dataset se-qa-holdout --metric recall@10 --knn 10 --norm none
```
output snippet: 
```
# fp16 export (reference)
recall@1: 0.61
recall@5: 0.78
recall@10: 0.842
silhouette: 0.21

# int6 export
recall@1: 0.54
recall@5: 0.72
recall@10: 0.780
silhouette: 0.12
```
notes: short queries (<=12 tokens) are worst; long queries less affected.

liam: did the export pipeline drop the final L2 normalize? that often shrinks cosine -> inner product mismatch with ANN index.

anya: good call — the int6 export log shows: 
```
WARNING: dropped layer 'l2_norm' during onnx-quantize (unsupported op)
```
so I ran the eval with --norm l2 locally (normalize in eval pipeline) and recall@10 improved to 0.811 (still ~3.1% down from fp16).

sandeep: interesting. that suggests two things: 1) missing L2 norm explains a chunk of the drop, 2) residual quantization noise still hurts cluster structure (silhouette drop). did you try per-channel vs per-tensor quant for weights?

anya: export used the default: int6 per-tensor symmetric. I can re-run with per-channel; takes ~30m to re-export & eval.

maria: also try whitening/centering on embeddings before index build — sometimes quant interacts badly with mean offsets. we have a small script: 
```
python scripts/whiten.py --in embeddings.npy --out embeddings.whitened.npy --method mean+svd --eps 1e-6
```

eval-bot: note: added run to evaluation queue: job_id=oply-int6-perchannel-2026-03-23-01

liam: one more thing — check KNN distance metric. if eval used inner product (dot) vs cosine that will surface differences if norm step missing. what's index config?

anya: index config: hnsw, space='ip', ef=128. we accidentally used 'ip' for both fp16 and int6 evals previously. after adding explicit L2 norm we switched to cosine by normalizing and using ip index (dot on normalized vectors = cosine).

sandeep: if per-channel int6 still lags, try tiny calibration set with Kullback-Leibler or MSE for activation quant. sometimes symmetric uniform quant at int6 yields biased activation tails. also test clamp ranges per-channel.

anya: re-run per-channel job is in progress. early logs from re-export: 
```
quantize: method=per-channel symmetric
max_abs_by_channel: [0.42, 0.51, ...]
export ok: size savings ~3.2x vs fp16
```

maria: if you get a run where recall@10 gets within 1% of fp16, that's probably acceptable for Dedicated customers. but we should capture a reproducible eval notebook with plots — UMAP cluster overlaid, silhouette, recall curves vs query length.

anya: agreed. I'm generating a quick notebook and will attach UMAPs. early preview: int6 (no norm) shows cluster bleed; int6 + L2 norm reduces bleed but clusters slightly compressed; per-channel keeps shapes similar to fp16.

liam: can you also dump a few failure cases (queries where fp16 returned correct doc in top10 but int6 did not)? helpful to see semantics — are they synonyms, paraphrases, or rare tokens?

anya: yes — sample:
- q: "how to reset password for azure cli"
  fp16 top1: "reset azure cli password"
  int6 top1: "azure cli installation issues"
- q: "best way to paginate sql results"
  fp16 top3 contains the canonical answer, int6 misses it

sandeep: looks like boundary cases + quant noise. Paraphrase-heavy queries are vulnerable. Suggest trying small bias correction at output (learned scalar) or using cached fp16 hot-queries for top routes.

anya: filing an issue for model-export: https://redwood-internal/issue/12480 (notes: dropped l2_norm, defaulted per-tensor symmetric int6). tagging export and eval teams.

maria: thanks. next steps: 1) wait for per-channel run and eval-bot results, 2) produce notebook + failure case list, 3) consider short-term mitigation (add L2 norm in inference wrapper if export can't preserve it).

liam: FYI — I patched the inference wrapper to force L2 norm post-export for any model that warns about dropped 'l2_norm'. small PR incoming. :thumbsup:

anya: awesome. will re-run full 100k holdout once per-channel run finishes and post numbers. thanks all.
